#Development Log

## 2026-11-20: Section 4.1, Straight Line Cluster Split

**Task:** "you can start section 4.1. the data should be a fixed set of points. as i mention in 4.1, it should be a cluster of blue dots surrounded by red dots"

**Changes (completed, all code generated by Claude Code):**
- Fixed dataset: 50 blue points uniformly inside radius 1.0 and 50 red points in a ring at radius 1.8–2.8. It is generated from a seeded PRNG (seed 375), so every visitor sees the same points. The gap between the classes is deliberate so the z = x₁² + x₂² plane in 4.3 can reach 100%.
- Page layout: sticky Threlte canvas on the left, scrolling text steps on the right (using the starter's `Scrolly`). On screens ≤800px wide the canvas pins to the top 55% of the screen and the text scrolls underneath.
- One persistent Threlte scene (x₁ → x, x₂ → y, z reserved for the lifted feature) viewed from above with an orthographic camera, so it reads as a 2D plot. This follows the earlier decision to use Threlte for the 2D plots too.
- Step 0 introduces the data. Step 1 shows a line with two draggable handles. Each side of the line is shaded with the class it predicts, and the text card shows an accuracy readout (percentage, bar, "N of 100 points").
- Accuracy scoring: each side of the line gets whichever class labeling scores higher, so the readout shows the best that line can do. Claude Code chose this so users only have to position the line, not also pick which side is which.
- Points use the starter's colorblind-friendly category colors (#4477AA blue, #EE6677 red).
- The step text is draft copy written by Claude Code, for the user to revise.

**Files Modified:** `src/data/circles.js` (new), `src/utils/linearSplit.js` (new), `src/stores/explainer.svelte.js` (new), `src/components/three/Scene.svelte`, `src/components/three/Axes.svelte` (new), `src/components/three/Points.svelte` (new), `src/components/three/SplitLine.svelte` (new), `src/components/Index.svelte`, `vite.config.js` and `jsconfig.json` (added `$stores` alias)

**Issues Encountered:**
- Threlte's default tone mapping washed out the point colors.
- In the first automated browser test, the page's JavaScript failed to load ("Failed to fetch dynamically imported module"). The cause was rebuilding while the preview server was still running, not the code.
- At 390px width the x₁ axis label was clipped at the right edge.
- Limitation: with this dataset, the best any straight line can reach is about 78% (brute-force search over lines). This may feel more passable than the spec's "will not be a sufficient result" intends. Not yet resolved.
- Limitation: on touch screens the canvas blocks page scrolling while the line step is active (`touch-action: none`), so a touch drag moves the line, not the page.

**Resolution:**
- Turned off tone mapping on the canvas (`NoToneMapping`).
- Restarted the preview server after rebuilding.
- Added more margin around the plot when fitting the camera zoom.
- The 78% ceiling and the touch-scrolling tradeoff are open for the user to decide.

**Testing (run by Claude Code; not yet tested by the user):**
- Node script checks: 50 points per class; max blue radius 0.99 and min red radius 1.81; all points inside the plot; the dataset is identical on reload; line clipping and half-plane region areas are correct. All passed. The default line scores 59%.
- `npm run build` succeeds.
- Headless Chrome (desktop 1400×900 and mobile 390×844), driven by script: scrolling to step 1 activates it and shows the line, and a simulated mouse drag of a handle moved the line and changed the accuracy from 59% to 62%. Screenshots checked for layout.

**Next Steps:**
- User review of the 4.1 look, interaction, and draft copy.
- Decide whether to make the dataset harder for a line (lower the ~78% ceiling).
- Section 4.2: animate the points up to z = x₁² + x₂² and enable rotating the 3D view.

## 2026-11-20: Thinner red ring

**Task:** "can you make a thinner red ring?"

**Changes (completed, by Claude Code):** The red ring radius changed from 1.8–2.8 to 1.9–2.3. The blue cluster (radius ≤ 1.0), seed, and point counts are unchanged.

**Files Modified:** `src/data/circles.js`

**Issues Encountered:** The ring was made thinner partly to lower the best straight-line accuracy (~78%). A brute-force test showed that ring width doesn't change that ceiling: rings of 1.8–2.8, 2.0–2.4, 1.9–2.3, 1.8–2.1, and 2.0–2.2 all give 78%. The ceiling likely comes from gaps in how the randomly placed red points fall around the circle. In a separate test (not applied), spacing the red points evenly around the ring with small jitter lowered the ceiling to 71%.

**Resolution:** Applied the thinner ring as requested. Whether to also space the red points evenly is left to the user.

**Testing (run by Claude Code; not yet tested by the user):** Dataset checks rerun and passing (min red radius 1.90, max blue 0.99, all points in the plot, deterministic). The default line still scores 59%, and the best line is still ~78%. `npm run build` succeeds. No new browser test; only the data changed.

**Next Steps:** User decision on spacing the red points evenly. Then section 4.2.

## 2026-11-20: Bigger, more random blue cluster

**Task:** "you can make the cluster of blue a little bigger and more random, so the linear separation between the two is less accurate"

**Changes (completed, by Claude Code):** The blue cluster now uses a Gaussian scatter (σ = 0.75), dense near the origin with a few stragglers, in place of uniform points inside radius 1.0. Points beyond radius 1.5 are resampled so there is still a gap before the red ring (1.9–2.3) and the plane in 4.3 can still reach 100%. Claude Code chose the Gaussian scatter and radius 1.5 after comparing options (below).

**Files Modified:** `src/data/circles.js`

**Issues Encountered:** Enlarging the cluster lowers the line ceiling only modestly. In a brute-force comparison, a uniform cluster scored 78% / 77% / 76% at radius 1.0 / 1.3 / 1.5, and a Gaussian cluster scored 77% / 76% / 74%. Uneven spacing of the red points around the ring still seems to be the main factor in the ceiling.

**Resolution:** Applied Gaussian, max radius 1.5 (best line ≈ 74%). Spacing the red points evenly is still available if a lower ceiling is wanted.

**Testing (run by Claude Code; not yet tested by the user):** Dataset checks pass (max blue radius 1.46, min red radius 1.90, deterministic, all in the plot). The best line is ≈ 74% and the default line 54%. `npm run build` succeeds. In the headless Chrome desktop and mobile runs, the line step activates and the handle drag changes the accuracy (54% → 64%). The desktop screenshot was checked.

**Next Steps:** User review of the new dataset. Optionally space the red points evenly. Then section 4.2.

## 2026-11-20: Section 4.2, Feature Lifting Introduction

**Task:** "we can move onto section 4.2"

**Changes (completed, all code generated by Claude Code):**
- Two new scroll steps. Step 2 introduces z = x₁² + x₂² and lifts the points. Step 3 asks the user to rotate the plot and points out the bowl shape.
- Lift animation: on entering step 2, GSAP tweens a `lift` value from 0 to 1 over 1.6s. Each point rises to its height z, with thin gray stems from the floor showing how far it moved. At the same time the camera tilts from straight down to a 3/4 view, and a z axis grows out of the origin with the label "z = x₁² + x₂²". Scrolling back to step 0/1 reverses the animation (points drop, camera returns to the top view) and the 4.1 line works again.
- Rotation: OrbitControls are enabled from step 2 onward once the animation finishes. Zoom and pan are disabled so the mouse wheel still scrolls the page, and the view is limited to at or above the floor.
- A faint translucent paraboloid surface fades in at step 3. The spec does not mention it; Claude Code added it to make the bowl shape easier to see, and it can be removed.
- Design decisions (Claude Code): kept the single orthographic camera instead of switching to perspective, so the 2D→3D transition is one continuous camera move. z is drawn at half scale (`Z_SCALE = 0.5`, display only), because the red points reach z ≈ 5.3, which would dwarf the ±3.2 floor.
- Touch handling moved from a CSS class in `Index.svelte` into `Scene.svelte`. Touch scrolling is blocked on the canvas only for steps where dragging does something (the line in step 1, rotation in steps 2+).
- The step text is draft copy by Claude Code. It introduces the new feature but does not yet address SPEC "Potential Areas of Confusion" #1 (why we are allowed to construct new features). Per the spec, that is waiting on the user's direction.

**Files Modified:** `src/utils/lift.js` (new), `src/components/three/Bowl.svelte` (new), `src/components/three/Scene.svelte`, `src/components/three/Points.svelte`, `src/components/three/Axes.svelte`, `src/components/Index.svelte`, `src/styles/app.css`

**Issues Encountered:**
- three.js OrbitControls sets `touch-action: none` on the canvas container when created, which would block touch scrolling over the canvas on every step, including step 0.
- Exponents (x₁²) rendered tiny and offset because the starter's normalize.css shrinks `<sup>` twice (75% font size plus `font-variant-position: super`).
- Limitation: on touch screens, steps 2+ (like step 1) block page scrolling while the finger is on the canvas.

**Resolution:**
- `Scene.svelte` sets the container's `touch-action` per step after OrbitControls is created.
- Added a global `sup` override in `app.css` (keep the size reduction, drop the font-variant substitution).
- Raised the z axis height so its label sits above the highest red points.

**Testing (run by Claude Code; not yet tested by the user):**
- `npm run build` succeeds.
- Headless Chrome, scripted, at desktop 1400×900 and mobile 390×844, with no console errors or exceptions at either size: touch-action is `auto` at step 0 and `none` at step 2; step 2 activates and shows lifted points with a tilted camera; step 3 shows the bowl; a mouse drag on the canvas rotated the view (screenshot changed to a side view); scrolling back to step 1 restored the flat top view, and dragging the line handle still changed the accuracy (54% → 64%). Screenshots checked for layout at both sizes.

**Next Steps:**
- User review of the 4.2 animation, bowl surface, and draft copy.
- User direction on how to handle confusion area #1 (constructing new features).
- Section 4.3: slide a horizontal plane in 3D with an accuracy readout.

## 2026-11-20: Section 4.3, Sliding a Plane in the 3D Graph

**Task:** "we can move onto section 4.3"

**Changes (completed, all code generated by Claude Code):**
- New step 4. A translucent yellow horizontal plane fades in, and a slider in the text card ("Plane height z", 0–6, step 0.05) moves it up and down. Points below the plane are predicted blue and points above are predicted red; the step text explains this.
- Design decision (Claude Code): a slider in place of dragging the plane in 3D. Dragging would conflict with the orbit rotation, and a native range input works the same with mouse, touch, and keyboard (arrow keys).
- Design decision (Claude Code): the plane uses a fixed rule (below = blue, above = red), not 4.1's "pick the better labeling for each side". This matches the bowl picture the text describes. With this data the two give the same answer for any height that scores above 50%.
- Accuracy readout moved into a shared `Readout.svelte` component used by both 4.1 and 4.3. At 100% the bar turns green and the note reads "All 100 points are on the correct side." This also applies to 4.1, though a line never reaches 100% there.
- Starting height t = 0.3 (64%). The first choice, 0.8, already scored 84%, which gave away too much.
- Rotation stays enabled in step 4, so the user can rotate while sliding.
- Step text is draft copy by Claude Code. It says a 3D linear classifier is a plane but does not get into confusion area #2 (linear in the features vs. curved in the original data). That is left for 4.4 and the user's direction.

**Files Modified:** `src/utils/lift.js` (added `scorePlane`), `src/stores/explainer.svelte.js` (plane state and score), `src/components/three/SeparatingPlane.svelte` (new), `src/components/three/Scene.svelte`, `src/components/Readout.svelte` (new), `src/components/Index.svelte`

**Issues Encountered:**
- Blue points seen through the translucent plane (and the bowl) look grayish-blue. Lowering the plane's fill opacity (0.28 → 0.18) helped but did not fully fix it.
- In the first browser run, the phone-size test didn't actually run at phone size (a shell loop didn't split its arguments in zsh). Rerun correctly; no page change needed.

**Resolution:** Kept the lighter plane. The muted blue under the plane is left as is for now; it could be revisited (e.g., hide the bowl surface during 4.3) if the user finds it confusing.

**Testing (run by Claude Code; not yet tested by the user):**
- Node checks: max blue z = 2.118, min red z = 3.626. Slider values from 2.15 to 3.60 give 100% (30 of 121 positions). Spot checks: t=0 → 50%, 1.5 → 95%, 2.9 → 100%, 4.5 → 73%.
- `npm run build` succeeds.
- Headless Chrome at desktop 1400×900 and phone 390×844, no console errors at either size: the step 1 readout still works through the shared component (54%); step 4 starts at 64% with the slider at 0.30; 52 ArrowRight key presses on the focused slider move it to 2.90, the readout shows 100% with the green message, and the rendered plane moved; 40 more presses (4.90) drop it to 58%. Screenshots checked at both sizes.

**Next Steps:**
- User review of 4.3 (plane look, slider, draft copy, muted blue under the plane).
- Section 4.4: two side-by-side 3D views, collapse of the right one to 2D with the intersection circle drawn dashed, and plane height/tilt controls. This is where confusion area #2 comes up, so check with the user before building that part.

## 2026-11-20: Section 4.3 revisions (user feedback)

**Task:** "make the plane a little thicker so we can see it more clearly from the side. add a 'slice' or 'ring' through the bowl so it is clear where the plane intersects it. for settling the confusing part, note this as something we have to fix later on and leave it for now"

**Changes (completed, by Claude Code):**
- The plane is now a thin slab (box, 0.08 thick) with outlined edges, in place of a zero-thickness plane, so it shows as a band when viewed from the side. Fill opacity 0.2.
- Added a dark orange ring where the plane cuts the bowl. Because the bowl is z = x₁² + x₂², the cut at plane height t is a circle of radius √t, so the ring follows the slider exactly. The ring is hidden when the plane is above the bowl's rim (radius > 2.5) or at the very bottom.
- `SeparatingPlane` now takes the unscaled height `t` and does the display scaling itself; removed the now-unused `Z_SCALE` import from `Scene.svelte`.

**Open item, deferred by user decision: confusion area #2.** The explainer does not yet explain why a classifier that is linear in (x₁, x₂, z) gives a curved (circular) boundary in the original (x₁, x₂) data. The user asked to leave this and fix it later. Planned changes only: none chosen yet.

**Files Modified:** `src/components/three/SeparatingPlane.svelte`, `src/components/three/Scene.svelte`

**Issues Encountered:** None in the page. In the browser test script, dragging the canvas to reach the side view took keyboard focus away from the slider, so later arrow-key presses no longer moved it. That is expected browser behavior, not a bug.

**Resolution:** N/A.

After dragging the view to a side angle, the screenshot shows the plane as a visible band with all blue points below and all red points above. Phone size was not retested for this change.

**Next Steps:**
- Confusion area #2: deferred; revisit later.

## 2026-11-20: Dashed intersection ring

**Task:** "try a dashed intersection line rather than a solid one"

**Changes (completed, by Claude Code):** The plane/bowl intersection ring is now a dashed line in place of a solid torus. It is drawn with Threlte's `MeshLine` (plain WebGL lines are always 1px and can't be made thicker): 3px wide in screen pixels, same gold #b88a00. Dash length is fixed in world units (one dash + gap = 0.22), so the ring gets more dashes, not longer ones, as it grows with the slider. This also matches the spec's dashed circle in 4.4.

**Files Modified:** `src/components/three/SeparatingPlane.svelte`

**Issues Encountered:** The first attempt set the width in world units with size attenuation on. With the orthographic camera, MeshLine multiplies the width by the canvas size, so the dashes rendered roughly 30px wide, as thick radial bars.

**Resolution:** Turned size attenuation off so the width is in screen pixels (3px).

**Testing (run by Claude Code; not yet tested by the user):** `npm run build` succeeds. Headless Chrome (desktop 1400×900), no console errors: slider 0.30 → 64%, 2.90 → 100%. 3/4-view screenshot shows a thin evenly dashed gold ring where the plane meets the bowl. In the side view the ring lies within the plane's band.

**Next Steps:** User review. Then section 4.4.
